# Add S3 datastore-based usage measurement

Measurement configurations need a `"datastoreBased"` mode for S3 ingestion. Its `measurementConfiguration` contains `platform: "s3"` and the customer's string `accountId`; returned and persisted configuration also includes the generated `iamRoleArn`, `externalId`, `ingestion`, `dlq`, and `region` fields. Omitted platform and region default to `"s3"` and `"us-east-1"`. Creating a measurement must provision a uniquely named IAM role and policy scoped to that business's ingestion and DLQ prefixes, trusting the customer account with a fresh external ID. Updating the account must update role trust while preserving that role and external ID.

The internal S3 connector posts `{ message, s3Key }`, where `message` is one standard usage JSON record and the first `s3Key` segment is the business ID. Valid records must flow through the existing usage service with that business ID. Malformed records must be written to the configured DLQ under the mirrored source key plus `.message.text`, with the failed input and processing metadata; already-relative source keys must work too. Existing API-, agent-, and infrastructure-based measurement behavior must remain unchanged.

Preserve the existing integration boundaries used by this codebase: implement S3 provisioning on `DatastoreAccessInformation.setupAccess`, trust updates on `DatastoreAccessInformation.updateAccess`, orchestration in `MeasurementConfigService.create`, connector delivery on the exported `PrivateAPIUsageController.dbUsage`, and generic DLQ delivery on `StandardMeasurementEntity.publishFailureToDLQ`. Use `DB_MEASUREMENT_BUCKET_NAME`, `DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME`, and `AWS_REGION`. The IAM role name is `datastore-<businessID>-<measurementId>`; its trust policy principal is `arn:aws:iam::<accountId>:root` and its external-ID condition must match the returned value. `dbUsage` passes the parsed record to `UsageService.create` with the business ID derived from `s3Key`.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure and existing patterns.

Done. `npm run build` and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` both pass (46 suites, 84 tests, lint clean).

## What changed

**Datastore measurement configuration** — `src/measurement-config/entities/measurement-config.entity.ts:427`
- `DatastoreAccessInformation` now carries `platform` (default `s3`), the customer's `accountId`, `region` (default `us-east-1`), plus the generated `iamRoleArn`, `externalId`, `ingestion` and `dlq`. All of them round-trip through `transformer`/`dbModelToEntity`, so they are persisted and read back.
- `setupAccess` provisions an IAM role named `datastore-<businessID>-<measurementId>` whose trust policy names `arn:aws:iam::<accountId>:root` and conditions on a freshly generated external ID, then grants it `s3://<DB_MEASUREMENT_BUCKET_NAME>/<businessID>/*` (read/write) and `s3://<DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME>/<businessID>/*` (read) through a policy of the same name. The generated values are set on, and returned with, the configuration. The old bucket-policy mutation is gone.
- `updateAccess` only replaces the role trust, preserving the role and the external ID already handed to the customer.
- `MeasurementConfigService.create` provisions before persisting and returns the resulting configuration; `update` refreshes the trust. API-, agent- and infrastructure-based flows return exactly what they did before.

**Connector ingestion** — `src/usage/usage.controller.ts:47`
- The controller is now exported as `PrivateAPIUsageController` (with a `UsageController` alias kept for existing importers). `dbUsage` derives the business ID from the first segment of `s3Key`, parses `message`, and forwards `{ ...record, businessID }` to `UsageService.create`.
- Anything malformed (bad JSON, non-object record, missing `s3Key`) goes to `StandardMeasurementEntity.publishFailureToDLQ` — `src/measurement-config/entities/standardMeasurement.entity.ts:107` — which writes the failed input plus processing metadata to the DLQ bucket under the mirrored source key + `.message.text`; fully qualified `s3://bucket/key` sources are made relative, already-relative keys pass through.

**Supporting changes**: `UpdateDatastoreAccessInformation` DTO + swagger models, `DbMeasuredusageDto` documentation, `@aws-sdk/client-iam` added to dependencies, regenerated private OpenAPI spec, and a small `src/utils/aws/awsOperation.ts` helper so an operation is sent through whichever flavour (aggregated method or command) of an SDK client is at hand.

**New specs**: `measurement-config.entity.spec.ts`, `datastoreMeasurement.service.spec.ts`, `dbUsage.controller.spec.ts` cover provisioning, trust updates, persistence round-trip, valid-record delivery and DLQ mirroring.

One note worth flagging: `@aws-sdk/client-iam@3.272.0` is present in `node_modules` without its own dependency tree, so its runtime config resolves against the much older hoisted `@aws-sdk/smithy-client@3.85.0`. Clients are therefore constructed with an explicit logger (`getAwsClient`), otherwise instantiation throws `NoOpLogger is not a constructor`. A `npm install` that properly resolves the IAM client's dependencies would remove that constraint.
